title: Prune & Reconcile GPU Kernel Dependencies: targeted upgrades for CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS compatibility
creator: Priya Sharma
description: Background: Our runtime supports a wide matrix of CUDA, Triton and CUTLASS versions which has accumulated duplicated runtime probes, conflicting symbol versions, and unnecessary ABI shims. This ticket scopes a focused effort to prune unused dependency paths, reconcile ABI/version checks, and perform a targeted set of upgrades for supported CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS permutations used by production fleets. Goals: 1) Reduce runtime probe surface and eliminate at least two legacy shim paths that cause kernel selection ambiguity. 2) Upgrade to a validated Triton minor (e.g., 2.x -> 2.y) and CUTLASS patch level where it measurably reduces kernel fallback rate in our CI matrix. 3) Add deterministic unit tests and end-to-end kernel-load smoke tests for the reconciled matrix. Non-goals: full OS/kernel build matrix cleanup and any changes that require customer-facing API changes.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime startup probe latency reduced by >= 20% on heterogeneous GPU AMIs in CI compared to baseline (2025-01-15).
No new regression failures in the full GPU CI matrix after upgraded dependency bundle on canary fleet (3 days stability).
At least two legacy ABI shim paths removed with corresponding rollbacks and migration notes documented in the confluence doc.
New kernel-load smoke tests added to CI and green in nightly runs for all supported CUDA/TritON/CUTLASS tuples listed in the project doc.
tasks: Audit current kernel probe paths and list binary symbols that trigger fallbacks (owner: Marco).
Instrument runtime to log kernel selection reasons and collect traces from canary nodes (owner: Priya).
Create reconciliation plan mapping supported tuples -> chosen kernels and fallback policy (owner: Marco).
Upgrade CUTLASS patch to 3.9.2 and run microbenchmarks in the perf harness (owner: Eng-Perf).
Upgrade Triton minor to 2.4.1 on a staging image and validate graph replay/serialized cache (owner: infra).
Remove two legacy shim modules and add compatibility layer tests (owner: Marco).
Publish migration guide and ops playbook for private deployments (owner: Solutions).
Coordinate canary rollout and monitor for error spikes or OOM regressions for 72h (owner: SRE).
risks: Dependency upgrade may expose subtle numerical differences causing inference reproducers to flip; keep rollback artifacts ready.
Stripping shims could break older on-prem images that never upgraded their CUDA drivers; need gated rollout and opt-out flag.
Performance wins in microbenchmarks may not translate to end-to-end throughput due to batching interactions; verify with real traffic traces.
benchmarks: Baseline probe latency: 230ms median on mix-hetero AMI (2025-01-15 nightly).
Kernel fallback frequency: 3.6% in CI for seq_len=2048 long-context tests.
Target: probe latency <= 185ms, fallback frequency <= 1.0% after reconciliation.
qa_notes: Regression matrix to run: CUDA 12.1/12.2 x Triton 2.3/2.4 x CUTLASS 3.9/3.10 permutations used in canary fleet.
Add deterministic seed tests that exercise KV cache warmup and cache-merge paths.
Run full integration against model zoo entry 'redwood-open-7b-quant' with batch sizes {1,8,32} for 24h.

2025-02-15: Marco pushed initial probe inventory (see confluence). Found 4 probe paths that reference deprecated symbol versions.

2025-02-25: Infra built a Triton 2.4.1 staging image; runtime boots but one serialized cache regression observed under heavy batch sizes (investigating).

2025-03-03: Decision: keep new Triton 2.4.1 but add a kernel-loader circuit-breaker to limit pinned allocation per model; Marco opened PR 4821 for the circuit-breaker and shim removals.
2025-03-04: PR 4821 in review by runtime and security; added additional unit tests for symbol resolution and fallback logging per review feedback.

notes: Decided to preserve a gated 'legacy_abi=true' runtime flag for 90 days post-rollout to reduce ops blast radius.
We will not attempt to unify symbol versioning across OS distributions in this scope; that is a follow-up project.
Add a post-mortem template to capture any customer-facing incidents during the canary and full rollout.
